subject: RFP: TAM staffing, escalation paths, and incident comms — detailed questionnaire
messages:
From: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@atlasfinancial.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@atlasfinancial.com
Date: Tue, 08 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: RFP: TAM staffing & incident communication — detailed questions

Hi Aditya / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As part of our vendor evaluation (financial services line-of-business), our procurement and security teams have a few focused questions about TAM coverage, escalation paths and incident communications. Below are the specific items we need answered for the RFP questionnaire — we need the completed section back by COB Friday (12/11):

1) Dedicated TAM resourcing: typical FTE allocation for a deployment of our size (8 active services, ~150M tokens/month). Do you provide named TAMs?
2) On-call / escalation: do TAMs cover 24/7 on-call? If not, what is your on-call follow-up SLA and how are urgent P1 incidents routed?
3) Communication plan: incident notification templates, severity definitions, cadence for status updates, and expected recipients on customer side for P1/P2.
4) Operational runbooks: do you share runbooks (redacted) for common incidents (KV cache corruption, network IO throttling, model performance regressions)?
5) Evidence & audit: sample incident logs, SLA measurement windows, and retention period for audit logs.

If you can attach a short matrix summarizing staffing (named/unnamed), hours covered, escalation chain and a sample incident notification, that will help our security reviewers.

Cheers,
Sam
Sam Jenkins
Senior Procurement Manager — Atlas Financial
procurement@atlasfinancial.com
(415) 555-0198

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@atlasfinancial.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, procurement@atlasfinancial.com
Date: Tue, 08 Dec 2026 11:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RFP: TAM staffing & incident communication — detailed questions

Hi Sam — thanks for the clear list. Attached is a concise RFP response and a one-page TAM/SLA matrix for your reviewers (Support_RFI_Response_Atlas_v2.xlsx, Redwood_TAM_SLA_matrix_v1.pdf). High-level summary here: 

- Named TAMs: We assign a named Technical Account Manager for customers on Dedicated or Private deployments at committed contract levels. For deployments at Atlas' estimated usage we would provide one named TAM plus a TAM manager.
- Coverage & on-call: TAM teams operate primarily business-hours (Mon–Fri 7am–7pm PT) with a separate 24/7 incident response rotation staffed by the Global Incident Response team (GIRT). For P1 incidents GIRT will triage within 15 minutes and escalate to the on-shift TAM and engineering within 60 minutes.
- Escalation chain: customer on-call (if provided) -> GIRT triage -> Named TAM -> Escalation to SRE/Runtime Eng -> Executive incident lead (if severity persists beyond 6 hours). See attached matrix for contact tiers and expected response SLAs.
- Incident communications: we provide templated P1/P2 notifications (initial ack, hourly status for P1, 4-hourly for P2) and a post-incident report within 72 hours. Templates are in the workbook.
- Runbooks & evidence: we can share redacted runbooks and example incident logs under an NDA or via the Private deployment secured folder. Audit logs retention defaults to 90 days; extended retention options available up to 2 years as a paid add-on.

Next steps: I’ve attached the files and propose a 30-minute follow-up call Thursday 12/10 at 10am PT to walk security through the matrix. Does that work for your team?

Best,
Aditya Rao
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0110

Attachments: Support_RFI_Response_Atlas_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet), Redwood_TAM_SLA_matrix_v1.pdf (PDF)

Quick replies welcome — Sam needs final by 12/11 COB. I plan to send the updated workbook this afternoon once we lock language.

Aditya / Neha / Sam — apologies for the slight delay. I reviewed the draft attachments and updated a couple of items in Support_RFI_Response_Atlas_v2.xlsx (sheet: Staffing_and_Escalation) and added a redacted runbook excerpt (tab: Runbook_Redacted). Key clarifications: 

- GIRT commitments: Confirmed — we can state operational commitment: 15-minute triage for P1 and escalation to TAM/engineering within 60 minutes. This is part of our incident response practice; financial SLAs (credits) are separate and only in the SLA addendum.
- Named TAMs: Confirmed. For Atlas at the stated scale we will provide one named TAM and a TAM Manager. Named TAM will be introduced during onboarding and listed in the TAM contact matrix.
- Runbook sharing: We will share redacted runbooks and anonymized incident logs under the NDA. For deeper access (full runbooks / raw logs) we require Private deployment or a signed limited-access addendum.
- Audit logging: Default retention 90 days in encrypted S3-style storage (AES-256). Option to extend to 2 years; encryption-in-transit and at-rest are standard. I added a short paragraph with the exact language for the RFI.

Sam — attached is the updated workbook and the PDF matrix. If the security team would like, I can join the call Thurs 12/10 10am PT to walk through the runbook excerpt.
